signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-10-03 reality-web agent-profile contact-form data-loss)
evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/realtor/[id]/page.tsx:22-28 — handleSendMessage(e) does `e.preventDefault(); if (message.trim()) { setMessageSent(true); setContactOpen(false); }` and NOTHING else. There is NO network call: the file's only imports are `useState` (react), `Footer, Header` (@/components/ui) and the MOCK_* placeholders from ./_mock (L9-11) — no SDK/mutation hook (no useSendMessage / useContactAgent / fetch) is present. The user's contact-the-agent message is silently discarded and the UI shows a success confirmation (messageSent=true) for a message that was never sent.

This is the same data-loss bug class as the previously-FIXED sell-wizard no-persist defect (#code-review-reality-web-sell-wizard-no-persist, documented at sell/page.tsx:151-157 — a Publish button that flipped `submitted` without any network call). The agent-profile contact form on the PUBLIC, SEO-indexed /[locale]/realtor/[id] route repeats that exact pattern and has not been fixed.

Impact: a prospective buyer who contacts an agent through this page gets a false 'message sent' confirmation while the lead is dropped on the floor. For a real-estate portal this is a lost sales lead — a user-facing broken path with silent data loss, not merely cosmetic.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the absence of any mutation call is confirmed by direct read of the whole import list + handler body; MEDIUM rather than HIGH only because confirming the backing reality-server contact endpoint exists (vs. is genuinely not built yet) was not done at runtime. If the endpoint does not yet exist this becomes a completeness gap on the same line; either way the shipped success toast is wrong.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only once the endpoint exists): wire handleSendMessage to the agent-contact mutation (mutateAsync in try/catch), only set messageSent=true on resolved 2xx, and surface an error state on failure — mirroring the report/page.tsx submit handler. Single-package reality-web edit, verifies with pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web typecheck/test + biome.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-10-03 reality-web public routes serving placeholder data)
evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/realtor/[id]/page.tsx:16-20 — the agent public-profile page is keyed by the `[id]` dynamic route segment but IGNORES it entirely: `const agent = MOCK_AGENT;` (L20), with MOCK_AGENT / MOCK_AGENT_LISTINGS / MOCK_AGENT_REVIEWS imported from ./_mock (L11). Every /[locale]/realtor/<any-id> URL renders the identical hardcoded agent, listings and reviews. No useParams()/id read, no SDK fetch keyed on the id.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/profile/page.tsx:65,268,346,384 — the user profile page renders `const profile = MOCK_PROFILE;` and maps MOCK_LISTINGS / MOCK_ACTIVITY / MOCK_REVIEWS. The file header comment (L8-11) acknowledges this: 'when real auth/profile lands, replace MOCK_* with live data via the SDK' — so this one is tracked-WIP, but it is shipping placeholder content on a routable public page today.

These are distinct from the realtor contact-form data-loss finding (same realtor file, different defect): this finding is about the pages serving hardcoded fake data rather than reality-server-backed content. The sell/report/edit _mock files are legitimate static form config (PROPERTY_TYPES, SELL_STEPS, REPORT_PROBLEMS) and are NOT flagged — only the profile/agent MOCK_* entity data is.

Impact: public, indexable routes (agent profile especially, since it accepts an id and looks dynamic) present fake identities/listings/reviews as if real. SEO and trust risk on a real-estate portal; the agent page additionally 404-less-ly serves the same person for nonexistent ids.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the unconditional MOCK_* assignment and absence of any id-keyed fetch are confirmed by direct read. LOW severity because at least the profile page is an acknowledged placeholder; the agent page is not annotated as WIP.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only once the SDK hooks exist): read the id via useParams, fetch the agent via the reality-api-client agent hook keyed on id, render notFound()/empty-state on miss, and replace MOCK_* with the live payload. Single-package reality-web edits, verify with typecheck/test + biome.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-10-03 reality-web report-page i18n gap)
evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/report/page.tsx:24-34 — the submit/status copy is a hardcoded Slovak `MSG` object (submitting 'Odosiela sa…', errorNoListing/errorRateLimit/errorNotFound/errorGeneric all Slovak string literals). The in-file comment (L24-26) admits 'This page ships its user-facing text hardcoded in Slovak (only the title/subtitle go through next-intl today)'. The page is under the /[locale]/ segment and the portal supports sk, cs, de, en (per frontend/apps/reality-web/CLAUDE.md i18n note), so a /de/report or /en/report visitor who hits a rate-limit/404/generic submit error is shown Slovak text.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/report/_mock.ts:13-50 — the REPORT_PROBLEMS radio-card labels and descriptions (Podozrenie z podvodu, Nespravna cena, Duplicitny inzerat, …) are likewise hardcoded Slovak, rendered as the primary form options regardless of active locale.

This is a specific, previously-unflagged instance of the i18n-gap class (the 2026-09-19 pass covered other localization sinks, not this page). Distinct file + distinct strings, so not a duplicate of any open finding; backlog.json has 0 open code-review-findings for the segment.

Impact: broken localization on a GDPR/abuse-reporting flow for cs/de/en users — error recovery guidance and the problem taxonomy are unreadable to non-Slovak speakers. LOW severity (no crash), but it is a user-facing correctness gap on a multi-language public portal, not a mere style nit.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): move MSG + REPORT_PROBLEMS labels/descriptions into the next-intl message catalogs (messages/{sk,cs,de,en}.json) under pages.report and read them via useTranslations, matching how title/subtitle are already handled. Single-package reality-web edit, verify with typecheck/test + biome.
